newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent weak, market awaits APIs, Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent weak, market awaits APIs, Iraq news.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were steady at lower levels on Tuesday after a small sell-off in the morning which brokers attributed to profit-taking from Monday's sharp rally.
September Brent was trading at $19.34 at 1155 GMT, 12 cents a barrel down from Monday's close, while August gas oil was $3.50 firmer at $175.75.
Dealers said gas oil was stronger because it was catching up with Brent's late gains on Monday.
"It is as boring as sin," one dealer said. "The spreads are a bit tighter and that is it."
Oil traders are awaiting news of the reemergence of Iraqi oil on to world markets.

An aid distribution plan which had been delaying the restart of exports was approved by the U.N. on Monday and analysts expect Iraqi oil will begin flowing in a few days, after details of oil contracts are sorted out.
Turkish officials said on Monday that Iraq holds around a million tonnes of oil in storage at the port of Ceyhan.
Part of Monday's oil price strength in Europe was also attributed to buoyant gasoline markets in the U.S. and further rebel disruption of Colombian oil exports.
Traders are also waiting for weekly inventory data from the American Petroeum Institute (API) which is expected to be issued overnight.
